policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders two words, 'a fiery law' (fire + law), which is the divided qere אֵשׁ דָּת; the undivided ketiv אשדת underlies the reading the note reports but does not adopt ('as otherwise read, were streams for them'), and the ASV text renders the divided form.
ASV has the plural 'nor knew he his own children', matching the plural qere בָּנָיו; the ketiv בנו is singular 'his son'.
